operator_io_quirks: Mixed-case identifiers: Entrepreneur_ID, People_ID, Money_Requested, Date_of_Birth; must be double-quoted in generated SQL.
Tiny tables (6 and 8 rows) — no sampling cap issues; original_values fully read.
Date_of_Birth declared TEXT (not DATE) so TS dispatches to String fuzzer, not Date; values are 'YYYY-MM-DD' text.
Money_Requested/Height/Weight declared REAL, storage real; TS Number fuzzer with scale from type args (none -> default).
FK entrepreneur.People_ID -> people.People_ID, parent exists, parent is PK (unique) — clean FK.
No NOT NULL constraints (notnull=0 everywhere) despite PK; sqlite PK on INT is not rowid alias here (declared int, PK).
No CHECK, no UNIQUE indexes beyond PK; no views/triggers.
All columns null_rate 0.0 in original; TS may still emit NULLs (String/Number samplers can produce None via dropout).
People_ID in entrepreneur has distinct=6 = row count, but values {1,2,3,5,6} skip 4 — FK not surjective onto people.
Investor distinct=5 < 6 rows: one duplicate investor name in original.
Table order: people (level 0) before entrepreneur (level 1) — FK direction clean, no cycle.
No self-references, no composite keys, no dangling FKs.
operator_ts_expectations: People_ID / Entrepreneur_ID: Number fuzzer, int scale, range [-10^s,10^s] plus +-1/+-2 perturbation; PK dedup keeps first occurrence.
Money_Requested: Number fuzzer, real; fresh draws uniform in [-10^s,10^s] (huge vs original 50k-150k) — implausible magnitudes drive FN on range predicates.
Height/Weight: Number fuzzer real; fresh draws in [-10^s,10^s] wildly outside 1.7-1.9 / 45-80 — implausible values.
Date_of_Birth: String fuzzer (TEXT), so random charset strings, NOT dates — kills any date-format query; big FN source.
Name/Company/Investor: String fuzzer, random a-zA-Z0-9() strings with contamination — implausible names, FN on LIKE/equality.
FK entrepreneur.People_ID drawn from people.People_ID final values with replacement — ties/duplicates likely, may help some joins.
p=0.2 default, whole-instance p=0 w.p. 0.3 -> sometimes pure literal-pool reuse (more plausible, fewer kills).
max_l0 cap (rng*30) means after ~30 fresh draws values repeat — creates accidental ties/duplicates (FP source on DISTINCT/COUNT).
String length range from elements (min..max+1) — short names like 'IV Cam' widen range; long names cap length.
No NOT NULL enforcement: NULLs inserted fine; queries with IS NULL / NOT NULL may flip.
PK dedup on Entrepreneur_ID/People_ID reduces row count below chosen size — COUNT(*) queries diverge from size.
Literal pool from train SQL may inject real company/investor names, partially rescuing plausibility.
